McLaren.summary: McLaren has fitted a brand‑new rear wing assembly that boosts downforce where it counts most, giving the car extra grip in the fast corners. The central bodywork (the “coke” cover) has been reshaped to smooth airflow over the engine, helping the car stay stable at high speed. Finally, the rear brake duct has been tweaked to improve cooling and airflow, which means the brakes stay hotter longer and the car can push harder through the final sectors.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has tweaked the front‑corner aerodynamics by un‑hooking the “drum” lip from the duct and re‑setting the camber angle. The change smooths the airflow into the front of the car, giving a cleaner front‑end and a bit more grip out of slow corners. In practice, drivers should feel a steadier, more responsive turn‑in on this weekend’s circuit.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has tweaked the front‑corner of the RB‑the car, reshaping the wishbone cover and tweaking the wheel‑area panels to make the whole assembly sturdier. The changes are all about preventing any premature wear or break‑downs in the high‑stress corners of the track, so the team can run the car harder and more consistently this weekend. In short, a more reliable front end means fewer worries about sudden failures and a better chance of staying competitive right from the start.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has re‑shaped the whole underside of the car – the floor, its edge and the diffuser – tweaking the brace layout and the little vanes that control airflow. The new shapes give a cleaner air stream and more consistent down‑force, so the car should stick to the tarmac better in fast corners. A slightly twisted lower beam wing also helps keep the rear stable under braking, giving the drivers a bit more confidence over the weekend’s tricky sections.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has trimmed the outer part of the front wing’s last flap and tweaked the wing’s inner foot‑section, plus added a fresh, optional flap to fine‑tune airflow. They’ve also introduced a new fence on the floor’s diffuser and reshaped the lower edge of the diffuser winglet, tightening the car’s rear‑end grip. These changes should give the car a cleaner aerodynamic “bite,” improving corner‑exit speed and stability on the track this weekend.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has given the car a full‑on “aero facelift”: the floor, diffuser, rear corner and wing all get fresh shapes and smoother edges, while the sidepod now channels air more cleanly. These tweaks shave drag and boost down‑force, meaning the car should stick to the pavement better in high‑speed corners and get a stronger launch off the start‑line. In short, Alpine’s hoping the new bodywork will translate into more grip and a stronger fight for points this weekend.
